question.text: A scheduled commercial bank has a net worth of Rs 600 Cr, CRAR of 9.5%, and net NPA of 2.5%. Considering only the three NUMERIC prudential thresholds (net worth, CRAR, and net NPA) used in the RBI eligibility framework for a currency derivative exchange trading member, how many of these three does the bank satisfy?

answer.text: Two out of three — net worth (Rs 600 Cr >= Rs 500 Cr) and net NPA (2.5% <= 3%) are satisfied, but CRAR (9.5% < 10%) is not met
All three numeric thresholds are satisfied
Only one criterion (net worth) is satisfied; both CRAR and NPA fail
None of the three thresholds are satisfied because all have been raised recently

explanation.text: The Logic: Check each of the three numeric thresholds: (1) Net worth Rs 600 Cr >= Rs 500 Cr — PASS; (2) CRAR 9.5% < 10% — FAIL; (3) Net NPA 2.5% <= 3% — PASS. The bank therefore satisfies two of the three numeric thresholds. The Trap: Even though the question is scoped to three numeric thresholds, full eligibility to act as a TM in the currency derivatives segment also requires net profit for the last 3 years. From the facts given, that fourth condition cannot be assessed, so passing two of the three numeric thresholds does not by itself establish overall eligibility. Note: All prudential conditions are cumulative in the underlying framework; missing any one of them — including CRAR here — is enough to keep the bank from qualifying as a TM.
